content: {"id": "1d48d98c-8023-409c-8f9b-351fe43f5630", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "On a Windows Server 2019 EC2 instance, AWS-RunPatchBaseline fails with 0x80070422 'The service cannot be started' and Get-Service wuauserv shows StartType: Disabled. Why can't SSM just start it, and how do I fix it?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "2fc66d26-75fa-4d19-8075-f13d4fb51069", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Windows Update service disabled SSM patch failures"}]}

{"id": "85e594b2-a4ea-4948-a3d8-a5c7fd6cf759", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Quick answer on the "why": AWS-RunPatchBaseline (and Windows Update generally) relies on the Windows Update Agent calling into the **wuauserv** service via the Windows Update COM/service APIs. SSM's patch document doesn't manage service start-type as part of its own permissions model — it just invokes the OS-level patching workflow, which expects wuauserv to be startable. If wuauserv's `Start` registry value is set to `4` (Disabled), the service control manager refuses to start it no matter who's asking — SSM Agent included — because that's an OS-level configuration decision, not something the patch document has rights or intent to override. SSM Agent runs as `LocalSystem`, which can start a Disabled service via `sc start`/`Start-Service` just fine *if* it's not Disabled — but it won't flip the StartType for you, since silently re-enabling a service an admin deliberately disabled (often via GPO) would be surprising behavior.

0x80070422 is literally the Win32 error `ERROR_SERVICE_DISABLED` surfacing through the Windows Update stack, which lines up exactly with what you're seeing.

**Fix:**

1. Re-enable the service start type (Manual is what Windows normally uses for wuauserv — don't set Automatic, as it's not required and can mask the real issue if something keeps disabling it):
   ```powershell
   Set-Service -Name wuauserv -StartupType Manual
   Start-Service -Name wuauserv
   Get-Service wuauserv
   ```
2. Check whether it's being re-disabled by Group Policy. This is the most common root cause in enterprise AMIs/golden images:
   ```powershell
   gpresult /h gpresult.html
   ```
   Look for policies touching `Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Windows Components > Windows Update` or any custom GPO/SSM association that sets `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\wuauserv\Start`. If GPO is reapplying Disabled, you need to fix it at the policy level, not just locally — otherwise it'll flip back on the next `gpupdate`.
3. If it's not GPO, check for a baked-in AMI setting or a prior hardening script (CIS/STIG benchmarks sometimes disable wuauserv to force WSUS-only or SCCM-only patching paths) — in which case AWS-RunPatchBaseline may be fundamentally incompatible with that hardening posture until you carve out an exception.
4. Re-run `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` once the service is confirmed Manual/Running.

Want me to check this specific instance's service state and recent SSM command history to confirm it's really a StartType issue and not something re-disabling it on a schedule?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
